title: Applied Materials (AMAT) Stock Moves 1.77%: What You Should Know
author: Na
description: Applied Materials (AMAT) closed at $472.46, up 1.77% in the latest session. The company is expected to report earnings on November 12, 2026, with analysts projecting $4.05 EPS (86.64% YoY growth) and $10.29B quarterly revenue (51.28% YoY growth). AMAT holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with a Forward P/E of 36.31, slightly above its industry average of 36.01.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong earnings growth expectations (86.64% YoY), positive analyst estimate revisions, Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating, and solid revenue growth projections (51.28% YoY) support a positive outlook. The company operates in a top-20% ranked industry, though valuation metrics show it trading at a slight premium to peers.

title: LRCX Eyes Mid-40s Operating Margin: Is the Long-Term Goal Achievable?
author: Zacks.Com
description: Lam Research targets mid-40% operating margins over the next several years, up from current 38.4%. Q1'27 guidance shows continued margin expansion with expected revenues of $8.1B and 39.5% non-GAAP operating margin. AI demand, advanced packaging, and higher-margin services are expected to support growth, though the goal requires sustained execution and disciplined cost management amid planned $3B R&D investments.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company is demonstrating strong margin expansion (38.4% in Q4'26), positive Q1'27 guidance with expected 39.5% operating margin, and multiple growth drivers including AI demand and advanced packaging. Stock has surged 76.6% YTD. Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating supports positive outlook, though valuation is elevated at 30.85 forward P/E.

Competitor showing strong margin expansion with non-GAAP operating margin improving to 34% from 30.7% year-over-year, and Semiconductor Systems segment achieving 38% margin. Revenue growth of 25% YoY demonstrates robust demand in the semiconductor equipment sector.

Competitor demonstrating impressive margin expansion with non-GAAP operating margin reaching 43.7%, up 110 basis points sequentially. Strong revenue growth and favorable services mix support margin improvement despite tariff headwinds, indicating healthy industry dynamics.

title: Global Chiplet Assembly Equipment Market Forecast to 2036 | Rapid Expansion of Semiconductor Assembly and Test Capacity is Reshaping the Industry

title: Applied Materials vs. Nvidia: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Erin Kennedy
description: The article compares Applied Materials and Nvidia as semiconductor investment options. Nvidia dominates with $215.9B revenue and 55.6% net margins but faces valuation concerns and AI boom dependency. Applied Materials offers more stability with $28.4B revenue and lower valuation multiples but slower growth. The author recommends Applied Materials as the safer choice, citing concerns that AI growth may slow and regulatory threats could impact Nvidia.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the safer investment choice due to stable business model, lower valuation on forward P/E basis (35.4 vs 23.9), strong financial metrics (0.3 debt-to-equity, 2.6 current ratio), and less exposure to AI boom volatility. Author explicitly states 'Applied Materials is boring and safe. Sign me up.'

Flagged as risky despite impressive financials ($215.9B revenue, 55.6% net margin) due to heavy dependence on AI boom continuation, potential slowdown in AI development, regulatory threats from Congress, customer concentration risk (22% and 14% from two customers), and supply chain vulnerability through TSMC reliance.
Mentioned as a critical third-party supplier for Nvidia's manufacturing needs, representing geopolitical and supply chain risk rather than being evaluated as an investment option itself.
